How do you check the credibility of a report on a highly complex subject where you are not very familiar with the topic area?

Ask a few people who are familiar with it, chances are if they all concur then the report is correct, and if you don't have access to other people familiar with the subject then you will have to do research on it yourself. You don't have to go fact-checking every single claim; a few random checks all turning out to be true should prove that at least the vast majority of the report is credible.

First, I do credibility checking. It is easier and more efficient to discredit an article than to verify its full accuracy. If I find glaring errors, two statements that cannot be true at once, or definitions that are obviously wrong, then I can safely say the article is not trustworthy.

Of course, this approach has a few dangers too. It takes time and caution.

As for verifying the full accuracy of the article, that is much more difficult.

There's probably no easy way, but here are some basic rules:

  • Always read different news sources on a topic.
  • Some of them are more credible than others, but there are no absolutely credible ones.
  • Read the Wikipedia article about it, including the history and comments.
